_comment: Surf fishing. Every figure here is from published sources, not first-party calls, and several CONFLICT between sources — those carry a `conflict` field and must not be published as settled. Two calls to DNREC resolve most of it. See CALL-SHEET.md.

headline.fact: Only five drive-on beaches need a reservation in 2026 — not seven.
headline.detail: DNREC suspended reservations at seven of the twelve crossings in 2025. Nearly every guide, forum post and blog still says seven are reservable. Getting this wrong costs a fishing trip, or a $107 fine for driving on without one where it is still required.

reservations.releaseNote: Weekly only — you cannot book further ahead than the current week.
notes: A no-show reservation stays valid, does not free the space for anyone else, and is not refunded or transferred.
Off-peak permit holders cannot drive on during reservation periods at all.
Print it. A digital copy is accepted as backup, not as the primary.

afterFour.rule: Annual and two-year permit holders can drive on without a reservation after 4pm, even on a peak Saturday.
afterFour.catch: You must be off the beach by 8am the next morning.
afterFour.why: This is the most useful practical fact in the section and it is barely published. Evening fishing on a peak weekend needs no reservation and no $4.

crossings.name: Beach Plum Island
crossings.note: North of Lewes. A prime black drum spot in May. Note: pets are prohibited here year-round, unlike the rest of the surf-fishing sand.

crossings.name: Gordons Pond
crossings.note: Separated from Herring Point in the booking portal after a 2023 plover closure forced DNREC to split them.

crossings.name: Point Crossing
crossings.note: The Point closes annually from around 1 March for nesting birds. Ocean side reopens 1 September; bayside not until 1 October.

crossings.name: 3Rs
crossings.note: The only reservable crossing outside Cape Henlopen. Has walk-on access too.

crossings.name: Key Box
crossings.note: Walk-on access; trucks tend to leave these areas to walk-on anglers.

crossings.name: Conquest
crossings.note: Walk-on access as well as drive-on.

crossings.name: South Beach
crossings.note: The big South Beach crossing lot is the best walk-on option in the state park system.

permits.note: Unchanged for 2026. The off-peak permit is being discontinued in 2027.

tiers.label: Senior annual
tiers.conflict: One source says seniors get no discount on the standard annual permit; another lists $80. Unresolved — do not publish either figure until DNREC confirms.

tiers.label: Senior two-year
tiers.conflict: Same unresolved conflict as the senior annual.

permits.free: Delaware firefighters and EMTs can get an annual pass or surf fishing permit free, applied for through their fire company or the Delaware Volunteer Firefighters Association.
permits.delivery: Permits take three to four weeks to arrive. You get a 30-day virtual permit to use while you wait, so a May purchase still works for a June trip — but only just.
permits.offPeakWindows: Seven days a week 1 February – 29 May and 6 September – 31 December. Monday to Friday only between Memorial Day and Labor Day, excluding Memorial Day, 4 July and Labor Day themselves.

offPeakEnding.fact: The off-peak surf fishing permit is being discontinued in 2027.
offPeakEnding.detail: DNREC removed weekend and holiday reservations from most surf fishing beaches in July 2025, which took away the off-peak permit's reason to exist. Almost nobody has published this.
offPeakEnding.openQuestion: Nobody has asked whether a two-year off-peak permit bought in 2026 stays valid through 2027. That is the first question on the call list.

exemption.rule: A valid surf fishing vehicle permit exempts the permit holder from needing a fishing licence — but only while the vehicle is on a designated Delaware State Park beach.
exemption.catch: Everyone else in the vehicle still needs their own licence. A father with a permit is covered; his adult son standing beside him is not. This is exactly what gets people ticketed, and nobody lays it out.
exemption.seniors: Residents 65 and over don't need a permit but must show proof of residency.

rules.label: Mandatory video
rules.value: Everyone must watch DNREC's instructional video before their first drive-on.

rules.label: Vehicle
rules.value: 4WD, minimum 7 inches of ground clearance, street-legal and registered, permit displayed.
rules.caution: The only source found for the clearance figure is a 2019 post. Verify before publishing.

rules.label: Multiple vehicles
rules.value: Each vehicle needs its own permit. Add them one at a time under a single account using "continue shopping".

rules.label: Sales cap
rules.value: None. The old 17,000-permit annual cap is gone.

noResidentPriority.question: Why don't Delaware residents get priority on reservations?
noResidentPriority.answer: The Division of Parks and Recreation takes federal Land & Water Conservation Fund money, which prohibits discriminating by residence — including preferential reservation, membership or annual permit systems. Anything offered to residents has to be equally available to non-residents for the same period.
noResidentPriority.why: This is the single biggest complaint in every Delaware surf fishing forum, and there is a real, citable answer that nobody publishes.

closures.headline: A bird can close the beach you already paid for.
closures.detail: The Point at Cape Henlopen has closed annually since 1993 for piping plover, least tern and migrating shorebirds — in 2026 it closed on 1 March. The ocean-side habitat reopens 1 September, the bayside not until 1 October. Closures can also appear mid-season: in 2023 a single plover nest shut part of Gordons Pond and forced DNREC to split it from Herring Point in the booking portal.
closures.consequence: Your $4 reservation is non-refundable and non-transferable. A beach can close between booking and arrival.
